# chat-demo

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A static chat demo powered by the DeepSeek API. No application backend is required: the browser connects directly to the configured API service.

You can [try the app online](https://deepseek-ai.github.io/chat-demo/) or download the archive from [Releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-chat-demo/releases), extract it, and double-click `index.html` to use it locally without installation or a build. Enter your API key in Settings before your first chat.

## Getting started

Install Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo.git
cd chat-demo
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:8090.

To build the static site:

```sh
pnpm build
```

The output is written to `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web server or open `dist/index.html` directly. Opening the file directly requires browser support for storage on `file://` pages and an API service that permits their cross-origin requests.

## Features

- Multiple conversations with automatic titles, renaming, and deletion; edit prompts, regenerate replies, and switch between message branches.
- Streaming replies, deep thinking, smart search, link reading, and source citations; stop generation or continue eligible replies.
- Upload, paste, or drag and drop attachments; use voice input and read replies aloud. A live audio spectrum appears in the first row of the input area while recording on mobile.
- Markdown, syntax highlighting, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams.
- Simplified Chinese and English, light and dark themes, mobile layouts, location settings, and chat history import and export.

## Data and storage

Your API key and settings are stored in the browser's localStorage. Conversations and original attachments are stored in IndexedDB. Local data is isolated by browser profile and site origin. Sending messages, uploading attachments, and using speech features sends the relevant content to the configured API service.

History import and export in Settings use ZIP archives. After confirmation and successful validation, importing replaces all local conversations and attachments. Exports include conversations and locally available original images, but exclude API keys, settings, and original non-image attachments. See the [history import/export documentation (Chinese)](src/services/chat/history/README.md) for the archive format and preservation details.

Settings → Data → Delete all chats clears all local conversations, original attachments, and unsent drafts after confirmation. It stops ongoing replies and returns to a new chat. Your API key and settings are preserved; files already uploaded to the API service are not deleted.

## Development

| Command       | Description                  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `pnpm dev`    | Start the development server |
| `pnpm build`  | Build into `dist/`           |
| `pnpm type`   | Run TypeScript type checks   |
| `pnpm lint`   | Lint with oxlint             |
| `pnpm format` | Format with oxfmt            |

[rspack.config.ts](rspack.config.ts) uses `https://api.deepseek.com` by default. Use `createConfig({ apiOrigin, devServer })` to customize the API origin and development server proxy.

Chat uses `deepseek-flash` by default through Anthropic-compatible Messages / Files APIs. Speech features use ASR / TTS endpoints. Requests include extensions for search, link reading, titles, and `latest_reminder`, so the configured service must support the corresponding capabilities. Supported attachment formats are determined by server-side validation.

```text
src/
  app/                 Application layout, themes, and global styles
  components/          Chat, settings, Markdown, and other UI components
  i18n/                English and Chinese translations
  services/
    api/               API requests, SSE, and protocol types
    chat/              Conversations, message branches, storage, and history import/export
    markdown/          Markdown parsing, syntax highlighting, and diagrams
    speech/            Audio recording and read-aloud playback
  utils/               Shared utilities
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The build copies the license to `dist/LICENSE`; include it when distributing the app. Third-party dependencies are subject to their own licenses.

T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/overview.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

The AI Orchestrator for 100x builders.
Run Claude Code, Codex, and any other coding agent in parallel, each in its own worktree. Chat or terminal, on your laptop or in the cloud, with diffs, a browser, and a CLI in one app.

Download Orca

### Orchestrate Agents Hand a big task to one agent. It splits the work, starts worker agents in their own workspaces, and brings their results back to you. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration)
### Run Anywhere Pair a Remote Orca Server, work on any SSH host, or give a worktree its own cloud VM. Your agents keep running when your laptop sleeps. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/ways-to-run)

[iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Android APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/mobile)

# ARTEX **Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.** (upstream: [Autumn-27/ARTEX](https://github.com/Autumn-27), AGPL-3.0) Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools, and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/BaaRai/ARTEX?label=release&color=6b34db)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](go.mod) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
--- ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets. - **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven. - **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two. - **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic; findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response. - **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates, token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output. - **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL, your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama. --- ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key) docker compose up -d --build # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL ``` Open **http://localhost:8787**. --- ## How it works ### Dual-graph architecture: exploration graph + asset graph ARTEX separates *what the goals are* from *how far testing has progressed* into two independent graphs linked by anchors: - **Asset graph (shared across tasks).** One source of truth for `root_domain / subdomain / ip / service / app / endpoint`, owned by companies. Parent-child relationships and deduplication keys are computed by the program; agents only submit raw observations. - **Exploration graph (per task).** The task's reasoning and progress: `goal / intent / fact / finding / hint` nodes connected by `spawns / derived_from / yields / proves` edges into a lineage chain. - **Anchors link them.** `exploration_anchors(node_id, asset_id)` ties intents, facts and findings to concrete assets: which assets a direction touched, and which intents tested a given asset. This also powers **asset test coverage** and the coverage graph. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph EG["Exploration graph (per-task · advance chain)"] direction TB G["goal"] I1["intent A"] F1["fact"] I2["intent B"] FD["finding (vulnerability)"] G -->|spawns| I1 I1 -->|yields| F1 F1 -->|derived_from| I2 I2 -->|proves| FD end subgraph AG["Asset graph (globally shared · source of truth)"] direction TB RD["root_domain"] SD["subdomain"] SV["service"] EP["endpoint"] RD --> SD --> SV --> EP end I1 -. anchor .-> SD F1 -. anchor .-> SV I2 -. anchor .-> EP FD -. anchor .-> EP ``` The **planner** reads the exploration graph, judges goals, and dispatches intents only when there is an uncovered direction; a **worker** claims one intent, executes it, writes assets/facts/findings back into both graphs, then stops. ### The engine loop The engine is event-driven: any graph change wakes the planner, workers claim and execute intents, write-back triggers the next round, until `prove_goal` closes the task. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant EV as graph-change debounce participant P as planner participant FR as frontier intent queue participant W as worker participant PX as recording proxy participant DB as dual graphs + activity EV-->>P: wake up P->>DB: read situation (graph_overview prefetch + coverage/scope) P->>FR: dispatch 0..N intents (with asset_ids) Note over P,FR: most wake-ups dispatch 0 (no new direction means done) W->>FR: claimNext claims one intent W->>DB: fetch the raw assets of the intent's asset_ids W->>PX: real tool execution (Kali / Bash / HTTP) PX-->>W: response (fully traced + CA verified) W->>DB: write back fact / asset / finding + per-step activity DB-->>EV: graph change EV-->>P: wake again (closed loop) ``` ### Durable attack chains, shared worker memory Real attack chains are multi-step and ordered (find an injection → get credentials → move laterally). The planner keeps a **todolist retained per task across wake-ups**: it records the chain once, then dispatches the next step only when its prerequisites are satisfied by facts. Workers can also **search each other's execution traces** (`search_all_worker_traces`, `list_worker_traces`, `get_worker_trace`). Observations that never became formal facts (an error message, a response snippet, a hidden parameter) are still reusable by the next worker, while each worker remains confined to the intent it claimed. --- ## Features ### Evidence, not chat logs - **Recording MITM proxy** (`:8788`) with a generated CA: every Bash/HTTP tool call is traced, and request/response evidence can be bound to a finding. - **Browser extension** (`extension/`) for authenticated targets: log in once (captcha, email OTP, 2FA included), capture the session, and the requests/responses land in the same traffic store.
Using the traffic capture extension - Load the unpacked extension from `extension/` (Chrome/Edge: Developer Mode → Load unpacked); - In the popup, set your ARTEX URL and token, then press **Start capture** on the tab you are browsing; - Use the site normally; text requests/responses are batched to `POST /api/traffic/ingest` (authenticated). Binary bodies (images, fonts) are skipped, bodies are truncated at 256 KiB, batches are capped at 50 entries; - Press **Stop** when done. Everything stays in your local traffic store.
- **Verified findings**: findings carry a POE level, a verification status and a note; a finding is `verified` only when a bound proof/response and verbatim evidence quotes support it. Gzip/deflate bodies are decoded before the quote check. - **Vulnerability retest loop**: a dedicated `retester` agent re-runs a finding with optional fixed version/conditions, records `Still reproducible / Fixed / Cannot confirm`, and can move the finding to `Fixed` automatically. Original evidence and reports are preserved. - **Reports and exports**: findings, evidence and task archives, with traffic snapshots kept encrypted at rest. ### Control without slowing down - **Interception gate**: every tool call can require human approval, with rules by `string`, `regex` or **argv prefix**. An argv rule is a JSON array of 1 to 8 tokens (Bash only, for example `["git","push"]`); it matches only a single simple command whose parsed prefix equals the pattern exactly. Pipes, lists, redirections, prefix assignments, subshells, background jobs, wrapper programs and command/parameter substitutions do not match; flags are ignored by construction (`["git","push"]` covers `git push --force`, but `git -C /repo push` matches nothing). Each approval records who decided: `human`, `rule`, `model` or `system`. - **Scope and target gate**: scope rows define the coverage denominator; assets outside the declared scope are not explored. The target gate (off by default, API-only) can refuse destinations that were not approved. - **Budgets**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a whole task (planner and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Near the limit the task enters a forced wrap-up; a worker is not started when the remaining budget cannot cover it. Budgets are in memory: a restart starts fresh. - **Noise governor**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE=quiet|balanced|aggressive` paces requests ARTEX sends to targets (per-host rate, burst, in-flight limit, jitter, backoff on 429/503, short GET caching). With a profile set, agents also receive low-and-slow flags for the installed scanners. - **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Disable with `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0`. ### Assets and coverage - **Coverage ledger and force-directed coverage graph**: in-scope assets are highlighted as tested or untested, with linked intents, facts and findings per node. - **Company-scoped asset graph**: shared across tasks, deduplicated by the program, with domain → subdomain → service → endpoint containment. - **ScopeSentry sync**: pull asset data from a [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry) instance by project or task, merged by company scope into the asset graph for agents to explore.
Syncing from ScopeSentry - On the **Asset Sync** page, enter the ScopeSentry address and API key; - Choose the targets and asset types by **project** or **task** (domains / subdomains / IPs / ports / sites / endpoints…); - Import: rows are merged by company asset scope and become part of the asset graph.
- **Task categories, templates, relations and archives** for repeatable engagements. ### Platform - **LLM profiles with failover**: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible relays and keyless Ollama; multiple profiles per task with automatic failover. - **Token accounting**: per-task and per-session usage, cache reads/writes, and an LLM record view for every call. - **MCP servers, skills, memory and a workspace**: extend the agent with remote tools and reusable prompt/playbook material. - **Single binary**: the Next.js UI is embedded with `go:embed`; PostgreSQL is the only external dependency. --- ## Installation > Requires **PostgreSQL**; exploration requires an **LLM** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or > `OPENAI_API_KEY`, also configurable in the UI). ### Option 1: one-click install script (recommended) ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX ./install.sh ``` The script detects or installs Docker, then offers **① all-Docker** (writes `.env`, runs `docker compose up -d --build`) or **② local build and run** (generates `config.json`, builds the embedded binary, starts it). Optional: `ARTEX_LLM_PROVIDER` (`anthropic | openai | openai-responses | ollama`), `ARTEX_LLM_MODEL`, `ARTEX_LLM_BASE_URL`, `ARTEX_LLM_PROXY`. **Base URL gotcha**: for the Anthropic format, enter the host **without** `/v1` (for example `https://api.anthropic.com`); ARTEX appends `/v1/messages`. OpenAI-format providers append `/chat/completions` (or `/responses` for `openai-responses`), so their base **does** end in `/v1` (for example `https://api.openai.com/v1`). **Concurrency**: work agents per task, in "System Settings" (default 3). **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results for the worker, planner, chat and main agent are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Unset or empty, the boundary is on; set `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0` (or `false` / `off` / `no`) to disable it. Cost: about 154 bytes per tool result plus one system note. **Noise profile (off by default)**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE` paces the requests ARTEX sends to targets (WebFetch, HTTP custom tools, the enrich probe). Unset or `off` keeps today's behaviour: no limit, no cache. `quiet` = 2 req/s per host (burst 4, 1 in flight), `balanced` = 5 req/s (burst 10, 2 in flight), `aggressive` = 20 req/s (burst 40, 4 in flight). A profile adds jitter, backs off on 429/503 (honours `Retry-After`, bounded retries, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only), deduplicates identical in-flight GETs and caches them briefly (60/30/10 s; never POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), and logs a per-host noise line each minute. `ARTEX_TARGET_USER_AGENT` sets a User-Agent on target requests that carry none. With traffic capture on, Bash commands that use the proxy (curl, wget, python-requests) are paced too, per host by the same rate and jitter, and counted in the same per-host lines. The in-flight caps, retries and cache apply only to ARTEX's own requests. This is best effort, not a security boundary. Raw scanners such as nmap are not paced, and neither is a command that bypasses the proxy (`--noproxy`, a removed proxy variable). With capture off, nothing launched from Bash is paced. The low-and-slow prompt block supplies the rate flags in every case. The **Target noise** card in System settings sets the profile at runtime (no restart) and shows the per-host counters; once saved, that setting takes precedence over `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE`. **Low-and-slow agent guidance (off by default)**: when a noise profile is set, the planner, worker, main agent and chat agents receive a code-owned prompt block with the profile's per-host limits and exact rate/delay flags for the installed scanners. It tells them to test one host at a time, back off on 429/503 and never raise the rate to meet a deadline. **Run budgets (off by default)**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a task's total spend (planner rounds and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Unset or `0` means unlimited. A worker is not started when the remaining task budget cannot cover its estimated cost (the average of finished workers, else 50,000 tokens and 10 turns). Near the wrap-up reserve (the larger of 5% and 20,000 tokens, and 2 turns) the task enters a forced wrap-up: the planner writes a summary and final goal judgment, and workers may only write back. The task then ends `done` if its goals are met, else `timeout`. Practical floor: below 50,000 tokens no worker starts; 50,000-70,000 typically gives one worker then wrap-up; pick well above 70,000 for real exploration. **Common flags**: `./start.sh -addr :8787 -proxy :8788` (`-addr` frontend/API, `-proxy` traffic recording proxy). ### Reverse proxy deployment (HTTPS / exposing only 443) The frontend, API and SSE stream share port 8787 (the binary listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default; the Docker container publishes on `127.0.0.1`), and the activity stream is same-origin by default, so **no `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` is needed**: expose 443 and keep 8787 internal. SSE keeps a long-lived connection with continuous pushes, so the proxy **must disable buffering**; otherwise the browser connects but never receives events. Nginx example: ```nginx server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ... location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; # SSE essentials: buffering off, long timeouts, HTTP/1.1 proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; } } ``` **Login rate limit behind a proxy**: login allows 10 attempts per minute per client IP. Behind a proxy every request comes from the proxy's address, so without further setup all users share one budget and an attacker who fails 10 logins blocks everyone, admin included, for up to 15 minutes. Keep the `X-Forwarded-For` line and set `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (comma-separated CIDRs, empty by default) to the address ARTEX sees the proxy connect from: - **nginx and ARTEX both on the host** (binary, `./start.sh`): the peer is `127.0.0.1`; start ARTEX with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32`. - **nginx on the host, ARTEX in Docker** (`docker-compose.yml`): the connection reaches the container from the Docker bridge gateway (a `172.x` address), not from `127.0.0.1`. Find it with `docker network inspect artex_default --format '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'` (the network is `_default`), put `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=/32` in `.env`, then `docker compose up -d`. For a peer in that list, ARTEX reads `X-Forwarded-For` from the right and takes the first address that is not a trusted proxy; from any other peer the header is ignored. Trust only proxies you run: a trusted peer can claim any client address. > Only when SSE needs a different origin from the page (e.g. a dedicated subdomain) should you set > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` **at build time** (it is baked into the static bundle during `next build`; > setting it at container runtime has no effect). --- ## Operations ### Backups `scripts/backup.sh` dumps the Postgres database (and optionally the data directory) with timestamped output and rotation: ```bash scripts/backup.sh --with-data # db dump + data/ archive, keep 14 scripts/backup.sh --keep 7 # db only, keep 7 ``` Restore into a running stack: ```bash gunzip -c backups/artex-db-.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T postgres \ psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" ``` Stored secrets (LLM API keys and proxies, MCP env, task credentials, notification channel config, Brave/Tavily search keys, web search and global proxies, the execution spec of custom tools) are encrypted in the database with the key in `keys/secret.key` (generated at first start, mode 0600, next to `jwt.key`). **A database backup without that key cannot restore those secrets**: back up `keys/` with the dump, separately. Deployments without a persistent disk set `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY` (32 bytes, base64 or hex, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32`). ARTEX refuses to start when the database holds encrypted secrets and no key is available. Daily cron example (03:20, operator crontab): ``` 20 3 * * * cd /path/to/ARTEX && scripts/backup.sh --with-data >> backups/backup.log 2>&1 ``` ### Updating and upgrading > Upgrading swaps the program and never touches data: the Postgres volume `pgdata`, `./data` > (traffic index, task files, transcripts), `./keys` (`jwt.key`, `secret.key`) and `./skills` are > preserved. **No manual database step is needed**: on every start ARTEX applies its embedded > `schema.sql` baseline, then any pending numbered migration from `db/migrations/`, in order, each > in its own transaction. Restarting the new binary is the upgrade. Back up `./data`, `keys/` and > the database before upgrading. **Update banner (opt-in, off by default)**: start ARTEX with `ARTEX_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to ask the public GitHub releases API for the latest tag, at most once per 24 hours (cached in memory; a failed check is not retried within that window). When the release is newer, the web UI shows a dismissible strip linking to Releases. The request sends only `User-Agent: artex-update-check`. Unset, ARTEX makes no update request and shows no banner. #### Upgrading from a clone made before 2026-10-23 The repository history was rewritten that day to drop a personal email address from the commit metadata. # SkillEvaluator ![SkillEvaluator wordmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/skillevaluator-wordmark.svg) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%20%7C%203.13%20%7C%203.14-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/skillevaluator.svg?label=PyPI)](https://pypi.org/project/skillevaluator/) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Documentation-docs.nvidia.com-blue.svg)](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2608.20614-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614) [![NVIDIA Developer Blog](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blog-NVIDIA%20Developer-76B900.svg)](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/) > 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI) SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and measures their effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill. Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Get started Three ways in, one CLI, same results.
1. Run the CLI directly 2. Add it to your repo via CI 3. Wire it to your agent
Install with pip: ```bash pip install skillevaluator ```
Or install with uv ```bash uv tool install \ skillevaluator ```
Then check your skill, no API key: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill --tiers 1 ``` Other tiers: [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). 		Our CI template checks every skill change. No evaluation code to maintain. Run this in your GitHub repository. It opens a setup PR: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` GitLab and details: [repository guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/repository-integration). Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent: ```bash npx skills add \ NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator ``` Then ask: *"Is my skill any good?"* See the [agent guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/agent-skill).
## Quickstart Both paths use bundled `text-analyzer`. | Start here | Requires | First result | | --- | --- | --- | | [Run without an LLM](#run-without-an-llm) | Git and uv | A deterministic quality score and findings | | [Use NVIDIA Build](#use-nvidia-build) | Git, uv, and a Build API key | Model-backed rubric scores and feedback | Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git, then get the example: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git cd SkillEvaluator ``` uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies. For standalone installation, see [Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). ### Run without an LLM ```bash uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality ``` No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores **88.8/100 (B)**, exits `0` and saves `reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json`. The passing threshold defaults to 70. This checks static quality; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path with your skill directory. See the [keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm). ### Use NVIDIA Build Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for **free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product). 1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment. 2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key. 3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check: ```bash export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...' uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build ``` The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in `reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json`. No agent runtime or Docker is needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds. The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the [Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) or [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx). ## Three-tier overview ![SkillEvaluator three-tier pipeline: Skill → Tier 1 Validation → Tier 2 Deduplication → Tier 3 Live Evaluation → Reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/three-tier-overview.svg) Each tier is independent. Add its extra to your command: | Tier | Question | Example after setup | Additional setup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Tier 1: Validation | Is the skill safe, well-formed and [harness-compatible](docs/tier1-validation.mdx#the-checks)? | `uv run skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm` | External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks | | Tier 2: Deduplication | Does guidance repeat or overlap? | `uv run --extra tier2 skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill` | Embeddings and chat; add `--catalog ./skill-catalog.json` for inter-skill comparison | | Tier 3: Live Evaluation | Does the skill help the agent? | `uv run --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill` | Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default) | Tier 1 fetches pinned, verified SkillSpector and Gitleaks releases when they are missing; Semgrep is optional. See [scanners](docs/installation.mdx#system-tools). `--no-llm` does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is `INCOMPLETE` and exits nonzero. [SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) provides specialized skill security scanning; [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor), the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs. Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See [tier guides](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/). ## Run the combined pipeline After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers: ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator validate ./my-skill ``` `doctor` checks readiness, not inference success. `validate` runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use `--tiers 1,2` to skip live evaluation or `--tiers 1` for static checks. `--no-autopilot` requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages. Tier 1 gates `validate`. Tier 2 gates unless `--no-block-on-dedup` is set; Tier 3 gates only with `--block-on-agent-eval`. Model and managed-sandbox usage can incur charges; see [runtime and cost](docs/tier3-live-evaluation.mdx#plan-for-cost). Standalone generation needs substantive `evals/EVAL.md` guidance, a `--prompt` file with task requests and outcomes, or matching retained traces. `--force` below replaces the autopilot starter; `--refine` refines it. Explicit `--grounding skill` permits skill-only starters. Review cases; templates omit unauthored negatives. ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full --prompt eval-guidance.md --force ``` ## Run from a source checkout Use `uv run --python 3.13` with the relevant extra. See [Installation](docs/installation.mdx#choosing-extras) for extras and standalone upgrades. ## Research and citation Resources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614), [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20614), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.20614), [BibTeX](https://arxiv.org/bibtex/2608.20614), and the [NVIDIA Developer blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/). Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff). ## Documentation See [the documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) for setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and [performance dashboard](docs/reports.mdx#performance-dashboard). ## Installation and third-party software Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation) to choose the full installation or a smaller per-tier setup. This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use. ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run: ```bash make lint && make test && make build ``` See [project governance](GOVERNANCE.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Support Support level: **Experimental**. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues); see [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md). ## Security Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub issue. ## Releases Release changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/releases). ## License Apache License 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
